analysis.title: JP Morgan Positioning Intelligence (Prime Time), 2026-10-02
key_insights: Equities have been resilient, but rotations under the surface show AI stocks still supporting the wider market while rate-sensitive areas and some cyclicals were sold.

The rotations benefited Quants. Performance was otherwise challenging because longs performed poorly in aggregate. Alpha bounced back on the short side, and crowding did better across regions except US Health Care.
US positioning was fairly stable (around neutral). Europe and China / AxJ saw the biggest reductions.
September month-to-date hedge fund performance is choppy at -0.7% (YTD about +8.1%). Equity L/S is the main drag at -1.5%, while Quants are up +2% to +2.5% on the month.
Crowding spreads were positive across regions in September: APAC +4.1% MTD, EMEA +4.6%, N. America +2.4%.
Health Care is the key crowding detractor in N. America. Biotech has seen the sharpest 60-day rolling de-grossing since early 2020.

Tech crowding bounced and hedge funds are buying US Tech. Mag7 was the most net bought theme globally (+3z over 20 days, mostly longs) and US Semis were modestly bought. EU Semis were sold (-1.6z MoM). Asia AI/Tech flows were mixed.

US gross flows stayed positive through the month and are at a seasonal high. The rebound from the Jul-Aug de-grossing most resembles 2022, with Quants driving much of the gross adds. Short flows could stay elevated into mid-October if yields keep pressure on risk.
The US Tactical Positioning Monitor dipped mid-September but ended the month roughly neutral (4-week change -0.3z, positioning around the mid-40s percentile).

Europe positioning slid from neutral to about the 18th percentile by end-September (4-week change -2z across CTAs, HFs and ETFs) and a tactical buy signal triggered. CTA positioning in Europe fell from about the 83rd to the 40th percentile.

APAC was net sold about 2z on the month by hedge funds (AxJ the main driver, Japan sold later). CTAs also cut Hong Kong (about 32nd percentile). China+HK positioning remains light (about 22nd percentile), Japan is back to neutral, and Taiwan positioning is below long-term averages.

Across US sectors on a 3-month basis, combined flows (HFs, retail, ETFs) show Tech bought (+3z) and Utilities sold (-2z). HF positioning is highest in Tech hardware and Semis, and most bearish in rate-sensitive sectors, especially Utilities and Consumer Durables & Apparel (which includes Homebuilders).
